content.caption: Grouped bar chart of WebArena-Shopping success rates for MaTTS (k = 5) across four memory mechanisms, comparing Pass@1 and Best-of-5 bars against a dashed no-scaling baseline line.
content.description: Grouped bar chart with an overlaid dashed line. It shows success rate on the WebArena-Shopping subset for MaTTS with parallel scaling factor k = 5 under four memory mechanisms. The y-axis is 'Success Rate (SR)' and runs from 35 to 60 in steps of 5, so it does not start at zero. The x-axis categories, left to right, are No Memory, Synapse, AWM and ReasoningBank. The legend sits at the top left inside the plot: 'No Scaling' is an open grey circle on a grey dashed line, 'Pass@1' is a pink square and 'Best-of-5' is a blue square. In each group a pink Pass@1 bar is on the left and a blue Best-of-5 bar is on the right. Each bar is topped by its printed value in matching colour (pink/magenta for Pass@1, blue for Best-of-5). The No Scaling result (the agent without test-time scaling) is an open circle drawn at the junction of the two bars in each group, with its value printed in grey next to it on the blue bar. A grey dashed line links the four circles and rises from left to right. Printed values: No Memory: No Scaling 39.0, Pass@1 39.0, Best-of-5 42.2. Synapse: No Scaling 40.6, Pass@1 41.2, Best-of-5 44.4. AWM: No Scaling 44.4, Pass@1 45.5, Best-of-5 47.6. ReasoningBank: No Scaling 49.7, Pass@1 53.0, Best-of-5 55.1. All three measures increase monotonically from No Memory to Synapse to AWM to ReasoningBank, and ReasoningBank is highest on every measure. Within every group Best-of-5 exceeds Pass@1, which is at least the No Scaling value. The Best-of-5 gain over No Scaling is +3.2 (No Memory), +3.8 (Synapse), +3.2 (AWM) and +5.4 (ReasoningBank, the largest). The Pass@1 gain over No Scaling is 0.0, +0.6, +1.1 and +3.3 respectively. ReasoningBank without scaling (49.7) already exceeds every other method's Best-of-5, and AWM without scaling (44.4) equals Synapse's Best-of-5. Per the page caption, Best-of-5 (BoN) is computed over all 5 trajectories and Pass@1 uses one randomly selected trajectory. The surrounding text points to the blue Best-of-5 bars to argue that higher-quality memory makes test-time scaling more effective.
